children: Meta Platforms Inc. (META, Financials) is the firm behind Facebook, Instagram and a burgeoning AI business and it is carving out its own voice in the Silicon Valley AI slowdown discussion.
Mark Zuckerberg doesn't believe everyone has to apply the brakes at the same time.

Meta's chief executive said it was up to AI labs to decide whether safety concerns are enough to limit progress. He cited Meta's own choice to postpone launching its Muse AI for months over safety and security concerns.
His reasoning is straightforward. Firms have lots of reasons to be careful.
They could be held liable if their models cause injury. Zuckerberg also thinks trust and alignment will increasingly be factors AI businesses compete on.
That puts him roughly in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's camp, who has similarly resisted a concerted slowdown. There is no universal consensus.

As artificial intelligence systems get more powerful, the CEO of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, has urged increased cooperation, and researchers in the business have issued increasingly dire warnings about the technology's perils.
Meta investors care about this argument since the company is spending aggressively to remain leading the AI race.

Zuckerberg's post indicates that Meta doesn't want to wait for the rest of the industry. The big question now is whether authorities will ultimately opt to let the corporations that construct the models make the decision.

title: Zuckerberg just picked a side in the AI slowdown fight
